competency: Inspect entries, bin contents and summary statistics of a TH1D instead of judging it only by its drawing.
acceptance: Visible tests distinguish entries from selected bin contents and verify at least one bin-level observation.

competency: Diagnose a histogram whose chosen range hides observations in underflow or overflow.
acceptance: A deliberately bad range produces observable under/overflow; the learner identifies and corrects the representation problem.

competency: Apply a numerical selection to a sample, fill only surviving values, and inspect how the selection changed the histogram.
acceptance: Tests jointly verify which values survive, histogram entries, range behavior and selected bin contents.

competency: Represent paired measurements with TGraph and inspect point coordinates.
acceptance: The graph contains the intended ordered pairs and tests validate coordinates rather than cosmetic drawing settings.

competency: Recognize why paired measurements with irregular x coordinates should preserve their actual x values instead of being treated as equally spaced bins.
acceptance: Tests use non-uniform x values so solutions that implicitly assume equal spacing fail observably.

competency: Use a TGraph to represent a small calibration curve and extract an interpretable comparison between measured and expected values.
acceptance: A deterministic calibration sample verifies coordinates and a derived comparison from the graph data, not drawing style.

competency: Represent a mathematical model with TF1, set parameters and evaluate it at selected x values.
acceptance: Tests verify model values before and after a parameter change.

competency: Diagnose a TF1 whose range or parameter configuration makes an otherwise valid model inappropriate for the requested domain.
acceptance: Tests include points inside and outside the intended modeling region and expose a parameter/range choice that changes interpretation.

competency: Fit a deterministic peaked histogram with a simple model and interpret fitted location and width.
acceptance: Fit parameters land in justified deterministic tolerances and feedback refers to model/data behavior rather than syntax.

competency: Inspect fit status and fitted parameters rather than treating a drawn curve as proof of a good fit.
acceptance: Tests require reading deterministic fit outputs and verifying the salient fitted quantities.

competency: Diagnose a plausible fit that is misleading because the model or fit range does not match the data structure.
acceptance: Two candidate configurations produce observably different fit quality or recovered parameters; the learner must identify the causal mismatch.

competency: Combine a peak and background into a composite model for data that cannot be represented by a single simple peak.
acceptance: The composite model recovers the salient peak behavior within deterministic tolerances and exposes failure of an under-specified model.
